chunks: Those who dispute God's revelations, with no authority having come to them, (are) greatly odious in the sight of God, and the sight of those who believe. That is how God seals every proud and perverse heart.
ai.seo_question: Why does God seal the hearts of the arrogant?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the spiritual consequence of *takabbur* (arrogance) and *jabar* (domineering behavior), where the lack of divine proof (*sulṭān*) leads to a sealing of the heart (*khatm*), preventing true acceptance of faith. It serves as a critique of those who dispute God's signs not out of sincere inquiry but from pride, a state particularly emphasized in the context of the Day of Resurrection when their arguments will prove futile.
